THIS CRL.P IS FILED U/S.439 OF CR.P.C PRAYING TO ENLARGE THE PETITIONER ON BAIL IN CR.NO.333/2022 OF KUDUR P.S., RAMANAGARA DISTRICT FOR THE OFFENCE P/U/S 376(2)(1)(n) OF IPC AND SEC.4,6 OF POCSO ACT ON THE FILE OF THE I ADDL. DISTRICT AND SESSIONS JUDGE AND SPL.
JUDGE, RAMANAGARA IN SPL.C.NO.142/2022.

THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY,
THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER
Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and learned HCGP for respondent/State and perused the material on record.
2. This petition is filed under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. praying to enlarge the petitioner on bail in Crime No.333/2022 of Kudur Police Station.

On completion of investigation, charge sheet has been filed against the petitioner for offences punishable under Section 4 and 6 of Prevention of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 ('POCSO Act' for short) and Section 376(2)(i)(n) of IPC.
3.

The sum and substance of the prosecution case is that the petitioner has committed aggravated penetrative sexual assault on the minor victim i.e. daughter of the first informant, consequent to which she became pregnant.
4. According to prosecution, the date of birth of the victim is 17.12.2006 as per the certificate issued by the school authority, which is however disputed by the learned counsel for the petitioner.
Learned counsel for the petitioner contends that the petitioner is innocent and he has been implicated in a false case.
5. As per the school records, the victim is a minor aged about 16 years as on the date of incident.
The medical report reveals that when the victim was subjected to physical examination, she was found to be pregnant of 22-23 weeks.

The statement of the victim recorded under section 164 of Cr.P.C. also Purushotham @ Purushi vs State Of Karnataka on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/108266699/
2 reveal that she was subjected to sexual assault, though the name of the petitioner is not specifically mentioned in the said statement.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The victim's evidence is not yet recorded.
Hence, at this stage, it is not a fit case to enlarge the petitioner on bail.

6. Considering that the petitioner is arrested and he is in judicial custody from 19.07.2022 and keeping in view of the relevant provisions of the POCSO Act, 2012, the learned Sessions Judge is directed to record the victim's evidence as expeditiously as possible.
If the victim's evidence is recorded, the petitioner is at liberty to move the Sessions Court afresh.
With the above observation, the petition is dismissed.

Sd/-
